lessons.title: Get customer input is the Lex block
lessons.why: There is no separate 'Lex block' to hunt for. Get customer input is where the bot is selected.
paras: You associate a Lex V2 bot alias with the instance, often with aws_connect_bot_association or the console, and then the block chooses that alias. The default quota is 70 bots and 100 V2 aliases.
On Connect Customer the worked pricing example charges 0 USD for the Lex speech requests themselves. You still pay for the voice minutes.
points: Branch on the intent name you configured, not on the sentence the caller said.
Slots are empty when the caller hangs up mid-prompt. Handle that.
DTMF and speech can both fill a slot. Test both.
A fallback intent should reach a person or a callback.
lessons.mistake: Building the bot in Lex and forgetting to associate the alias with the instance.

lessons.title: Slots become attributes or they vanish
lessons.why: The agent cannot see a slot you did not copy.
paras: After Lex returns, copy the slot values into contact attributes with names the CRM expects. Confirm the slot was filled. An empty slot with a successful intent is normal when the question was optional.
Session attributes can pass context into the next Lex turn. They are not a database.
points: Validate the account id in Lambda. Do not trust a spoken string as authorization.
Barge-in and touchtone buffering change what the caller can interrupt.
Log the intent and the confidence behavior you actually configured.
Keep the bot alias stable. Pointing production at a draft alias is how Friday breaks.

lessons.title: Fallback is a route, not a failure
lessons.why: Callers who say something unexpected are still customers.
paras: Point the fallback intent at a short prompt and a queue, or at a callback when the queue is long. Looping the same question more than twice trains people to hang up.
Use Check queue status or Get metrics if you want the fallback to behave differently when nobody is staffed.
points: Timeout and error are different from fallback. Connect them separately.
A DTMF escape key should exist even in a speech bot.
Test with noise, with silence, and with an accent the bot has not heard.
Do not send fallback into another bot with no exit.
